subject: Charter Citizen Participation and Recall Provisions
overview: The Article 8 subcommittee held its first meeting to discuss draft language for the citizen participation section of a proposed new city charter. Members deliberated on mechanisms for free petitions, ballot initiatives, and the potential inclusion of a recall process for elected officials.

items.title: Discussion of Working Draft
items.summary: Chair Milva McDonald introduced a working draft for Article 8 based on a generic modern charter and comparative language from Melrose, Pittsfield, and Weymouth.

items.title: Free Petition Provisions
items.summary: The subcommittee expressed support for a "free petition" provision to allow residents to place items on city agendas, tentatively proposing a 100-signature threshold and a six-month limit on repeated topics.

items.title: Citizen Initiatives and Referendums
items.summary: Members reviewed procedures for citizens to propose or protest ordinances via ballot, requesting that the Collins Center provide research on the frequency and impact of these measures in other cities.

items.title: Recall of Elected Officials
items.summary: The committee debated including a recall process in the charter, with members reaching a consensus that such a mechanism should be available but designed to prevent political misuse through high signature requirements.

items.title: Turnout Thresholds and Ballot Conflicts
items.summary: Discussion covered minimum voter turnout percentages required for special elections and established protocols for resolving conflicting successful ballot initiatives.

items.title: Public Engagement and Meeting Notices
items.summary: Eunice Browne proposed adding charter language to mandate broader meeting notifications and digital transparency, ensuring residents are informed beyond the minimum requirements of state open meeting law.
